Scope Doubles as Write Permission

Lesson 3's "read before write" 404 pattern turns out to already be exactly the check an update/delete route needs.

Lesson 3's updateTicket/deleteTicket controllers already called getTicketById first, purely to turn a missing ticket into a clean 404 before ever calling Prisma's own update/delete (the "read before write" topic). That call didn't need to change shape at all to also become this lesson's authorization check — it just needed the viewer argument getTicketById already gained two slides ago:

// Figure 4.13: one existence check, now also an authorization check (src/controllers/ticket.controller.js, excerpt)
export const updateTicket = asyncHandler(async (req, res) => {
  const existing = await ticketService.getTicketById(req.params.id, req.user);

  if (!existing) {
    throw new ApiError(404, `Ticket ${req.params.id} not found`);
  }

  const ticket = await ticketService.updateTicket(req.params.id, req.body);
  sendResource(res, ticket);
});

authorize('agent', 'admin') (route-level, previous topic) already guarantees a customer never reaches this function at all. What it can't guarantee is that the agent who did reach it is allowed to touch this specific ticket — an agent's scopeForViewer fragment only covers their own assigned queue plus the unclaimed pool, not every ticket in the system. getTicketById(req.params.id, req.user) already applies exactly that scope (previous slide), so an agent PATCHing a ticket that exists, but belongs to a different agent's queue, gets back null here — the identical 404 as a ticket that doesn't exist at all. deleteTicket follows the same shape.

Nothing about this pattern is new; it's the same function, called the same way, that was already there. The only thing that changed is what getTicketById itself now means once it takes a viewer — "exists" and "exists and you're allowed to see it" collapsed into the same question, so every caller that was already asking the first question got the second one for free.
